## Executive summary

This report analyses public daily mean discharge observations from USGS site `USGS-01491000` (Choptank River near Greensboro, Maryland). It demonstrates a reproducible time-series workflow. It does **not** directly measure biodiversity, and it should not be interpreted as a biodiversity assessment.

Run `source("run_all.R")` from the repository root before rendering this report.

## Data and provenance

```{r}
manifest_path <- "../outputs/tables/data_manifest.csv"
if (!file.exists(manifest_path)) manifest_path <- "outputs/tables/data_manifest.csv"
if (file.exists(manifest_path)) {
  knitr::kable(readr::read_csv(manifest_path, show_col_types = FALSE))
} else {
  cat("Data manifest not found. Run the pipeline first.")
}
```

The data are retrieved from the USGS Water Data API using the USGS-maintained `dataRetrieval` package. The raw download is retained separately from processed tables so the analysis can be audited.

## Data quality

```{r}
qc_path <- "../outputs/tables/quality_checks.csv"
if (!file.exists(qc_path)) qc_path <- "outputs/tables/quality_checks.csv"
if (file.exists(qc_path)) knitr::kable(readr::read_csv(qc_path, show_col_types = FALSE))
```

Review missingness and changes in sampling/record coverage before interpreting trends. Monthly and annual averages smooth short-term extremes.

## Seasonal structure

```{r}
fig <- "../outputs/figures/02_monthly_seasonality.png"
if (file.exists(fig)) knitr::include_graphics(fig) else cat("Run the pipeline to generate the seasonal plot.")
```

Seasonality describes recurring within-year variation. It is distinct from a long-term trend.

## Long-term trend

```{r}
fig <- "../outputs/figures/03_annual_trend.png"
if (file.exists(fig)) knitr::include_graphics(fig) else cat("Run the pipeline to generate the trend plot.")
```

```{r}
tab <- "../outputs/tables/trend_results.csv"
if (file.exists(tab)) knitr::kable(readr::read_csv(tab, show_col_types = FALSE))
```

Mann–Kendall tests for monotonic association with time; Sen's slope estimates a robust median slope. Serial correlation can affect test calibration, so the result should be treated as a first-pass analysis rather than a final hydrological inference.

## Smooth trend and seasonality

```{r}
fig <- "../outputs/figures/04_gam_trend_seasonality.png"
if (file.exists(fig)) knitr::include_graphics(fig) else cat("Run the pipeline to generate the GAM plot.")
```

The GAM allows a nonlinear smooth over time and a cyclic seasonal effect. The response is transformed as `log(1 + discharge)` to reduce the influence of very high-flow observations.

## Candidate change points

```{r}
fig <- "../outputs/figures/05_change_points.png"
if (file.exists(fig)) knitr::include_graphics(fig) else cat("Run the pipeline to generate the change-point plot.")
```

```{r}
tab <- "../outputs/tables/change_points.csv"
if (file.exists(tab)) knitr::kable(readr::read_csv(tab, show_col_types = FALSE))
```

These are candidate breaks in seasonally adjusted observations. They are not evidence of a specific flood, infrastructure change, or ecological cause. Follow-up work should compare dates with station metadata, known events, and data-quality records.

## Forecast comparison

```{r}
fig <- "../outputs/figures/06_forecast_holdout.png"
if (file.exists(fig)) knitr::include_graphics(fig) else cat("Run the pipeline to generate the forecast plot.")
```

```{r}
tab <- "../outputs/tables/forecast_metrics.csv"
if (file.exists(tab)) knitr::kable(readr::read_csv(tab, show_col_types = FALSE))
```

Forecasts are evaluated on the final chronological holdout. The seasonal-naive model is a necessary baseline: ARIMA should only be considered useful if it improves holdout performance. The current implementation fills missing monthly values for the forecasting demonstration; this simplification should be revisited before any operational use.

## Potential anomalies

```{r}
fig <- "../outputs/figures/07_anomalies.png"
if (file.exists(fig)) knitr::include_graphics(fig) else cat("Run the pipeline to generate the anomaly plot.")
```

An anomaly is an observation unusual relative to the chosen reference pattern, not necessarily an error or an ecological warning. Every flagged observation requires context.

## Limitations and next steps

1. This is a single-site hydrological case study, not an eDNA biodiversity time series.
2. Discharge is skewed and autocorrelated; trend inference should include sensitivity analyses.
3. A single-site trend cannot be generalized to all US rivers.
4. Change-point algorithms can identify statistical shifts without explaining them.
5. Forecast results depend on data quality, holdout length, and model assumptions.
6. A biodiversity-focused extension should use repeated species/eDNA observations, account for sampling effort and detectability, and join environmental covariates only when dates/sites align.
